mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the head and spine to the trunk was most worthwhile: it connected nerves and blood supply to the muscles and other organs built earlier.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the lymph network was less engaging: its vein junction had already been built, so aligning it felt mostly like placement.

surprise.text: The joined trunk showed that the diaphragm separates chest and abdomen, while the food pipe, nerves and vessels still cross between them.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though the later choices were mostly the only offered combinations rather than decisions I had to figure out.

continue.text: Probably not immediately. The completed body is a satisfying endpoint, but the final sequence involved several predictable fittings.
